storage: Keep in an airtight jar away from damp and strong smells at room temperature; it keeps for many months if dry.
looksLike: Very fine, bright white powder that squeaks when rubbed between the fingers and feels silky, not gritty. In India it is sold as "corn flour" but it is pure corn starch, not the yellow makki ka atta.
howToPick: Check the pack says corn starch / corn flour and not maize atta; if you avoid gluten, check the label for wheat starch or "may contain wheat" (as the dish 28 notes). The powder should be bone dry, pure white and free of lumps, with no musty smell.
shelfLife: Typically a year or more sealed in a dry pouch (general guidance; not taken from a source in this run).

usedIn.raw: 8 g per serving (1 tbsp), sprinkled over the marinated chicken with rice flour just before frying
